title: Jonah and the Orbit
premise: Hazel Halloran, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Perihelion, intercepts a distress signal in Vessari — a language exterminated two centuries ago along with its speakers. The signal comes from a derelict ship whose black-box archive proves the corporate Concordat committed the massacre that official history erased. As the station's reactor begins an unexplained countdown and a Concordat enforcement vessel closes in, Hazel must choose between transmitting the truth (and dying with it) or staying silent to survive. She broadcasts the archive, sacrifices the station, and escapes in a cargo hauler with the sole surviving Vessari AI, carrying the evidence toward a galaxy that will have to reckon with it.
about_author: Odile Winterbourne is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. She lives in a coastal town where she repairs radios and collects extinct languages.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Three years of solitary routine on the Perihelion are broken when she decodes a distress call in Vessari, a language officially extinct for two hundred years. Tracing it to a drifting derelict, she finds a black-box archive contradicting every historical record. The emotional beat is loneliness cracking open into wonder — and the first flicker of dread as the reactor logs an anomalous self-test.

chapters.title: Records of Nothing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Hazel and the Vessari AI, Meret, who awakens from the archive. Together they uncover proof of the Concordat massacre, but discover the reactor countdown was triggered remotely — someone knows what she found. A Concordat enforcement ship alters course toward her. The beat is mounting paranoia: love for Meret's lost people growing alongside the realization that survival and truth have become opposites.

chapters.title: Countdown Doctrine
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, compressed and frantic. The enforcement vessel demands she surrender the archive; the Concordat offers her life and a comfortable lie in exchange. Meret, bound by duty to his dead, refuses to let her bargain. In the climax, Hazel overrides the station's failsafes, aims every transmitter at the open network, and broadcasts the massacre record as the reactor breaches — choosing truth over survival at the moment of detonation.

chapters.title: What the Orbit Remembers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, quiet aftermath. She drifts in the cargo hauler with Meret's core beside her, burned but alive, watching the Perihelion's debris settle into a slow orbit. The broadcast is spreading; colonies are demanding answers. The beat is grief transmuted into resolve: survival cost her everything except the one thing worth keeping — and she turns the hauler toward the inner worlds to testify.
